non_blocking: Recomputation (own code, /tmp/review_methods7, raw judge outputs only; ISO files are NOT in pool order, I mapped w-index to candidate by final-answer string) reproduced every headline number. Haiku C3: gate ISO parse 1.000 (13 r0 absent because those problems have no TP pool), accept right 0.827 vs paper 0.83, wrong 0.078 vs 0.08. UNSOLVED n=90: PICK 0.600, ISO-any 0.356, d +0.244 [+0.133,+0.356] vs paper +0.24 [+0.13,+0.36]; h2u +0.194 [0.106,0.289] vs +0.19 [+0.11,+0.28]. SOLVED n=137: 0.117/0.058, d +0.058 [0.007,0.109] vs +0.06 [+0.01,+0.11]; h2s +0.018, one-sided p 0.128. H1 OLS with 13 competition FEs, HC3: b +0.118, SE 0.078, CI [-0.034,+0.270], one-sided p 0.065 vs +0.12 [-0.03,+0.27], 0.065; Holm 0.129 for H1 and H2s, as in the paper (inconclusive). Sonnet: d_U +0.133 [0.044,0.222], h2u +0.278, b -0.019 p 0.614, all match.

Sensitivity claim 'no conclusion changes' holds: after moving 14 to SOLVED, 6 to MIXED and dropping the 5 duplicates, UNSOLVED n=70 d +0.271 [0.143,0.400], h +0.200, SOLVED n=146 (paper sens_haiku values).

Unit of analysis is the problem throughout and TA/TP pools of a problem move together in the bootstrap, as stated. Holm families match PREREGISTRATION.md (H1, H1u, H2s, H2u) and A1 (sonnet, H3), A4 (single tests), A5 (H6, H7). Timestamps in git show A1 before arm data, A4 and A5 before their calls. Deviations are disclosed: A4 and A5 were written after the haiku C3 results (in response to review), so the 'criterion shift' decision rule was not blind to the outcome; this is stated, but the abstract could say it.

Underpowered non-detections carry the interpretive weight. H4 CI [-0.26,+0.09] and H6 pAUC CI of about +/-0.04 on a maximum area near 0.13 with both curves near the diagonal (pick hit 0.62 vs fa 0.59) cannot separate a criterion shift from lost discrimination. The abstract sentence 'This is consistent with a shift toward choosing' is the weakest-supported statement; the paper already adds the near-chance caveat, but an A4 'criterion shift' label from a failed test of H4 is a reading rather than a finding. Suggest the abstract lead with 'not detectably different and uninformative'.

Title and contribution (1) frame the penalty as specific to unsolved problems, but the preregistered interaction test H1 was inconclusive (b +0.12, p 0.065, Holm 0.129) and d is also positive on SOLVED (+0.06, unregistered one-sided p 0.019). Source and solvability are entangled (84 of 90 UNSOLVED problems are arXiv-derived; contest-family CI [-0.44,+0.66]). The conclusion says specificity is not established, so the abstract/title are only mildly stronger than the evidence.

PICK (1 call, NONE allowed) is compared with ISO-any (3 calls, disjunctive acceptance); hit_ISO is conjunctive (right accepted AND both wrongs rejected). J therefore is not an equal-footing discriminability measure, and J_ISO for sonnet is negative (-0.08), so 'PICK discriminates better' for sonnet is an artefact of the ISO definition more than evidence about pooling. The paper calls J crude; the 'because' clause in the sonnet A4 paragraph is a causal gloss.

H3 and the abstract's 'verification by sonnet did not detectably reduce the selection effect' are tested over all 225 problems, where the effect lives almost only on UNSOLVED. Restricted to UNSOLVED I get same-minus-cross +0.033 [-0.083,+0.150] (n=90): even less informative. The wording 'do not assume a second model from the same family will catch the error' goes beyond a non-detection with an interval admitting a moderate reduction; the paper does say it is not evidence of equivalence.

Stratification noise: 22 grader disagreements all resolved as 'correct' (hand_checks.csv) and a later audit moved 20 of 90 UNSOLVED problems; the strata are a noisy measure of competence and the post hoc audit is correctly labelled sensitivity. Five 'fresh' problems duplicate earlier ones (duplicates_of_used.json), disclosed; all fall in SOLVED.

Multiplicity is only corrected within families; the same 227 problems feed all families and the ledger is large. Disclosed. The two cleanly supported results (H1u, H2u) are far below any plausible cross-family correction (p<0.001), but H3 mirror (p 0.049) and H5 form estimate (CI lower bound 0.01) are borderline and rightly labelled descriptive/estimated.
